methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $41M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
First Resonance is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $41M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable, all operating in the robotics and manufacturing sector at Series A through Series B stages. Key private peers include Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for current valuation, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yielding $82M. Peer-median analysis across the four same-sector comparables yields a $1.7B implied valuation, with the comp set ranging from $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The peer median reflects the later-stage concentration of the comp set; three of four sampled peers are Series B.

The triangulated range spans $69M to $2.0B, with a median of $891M. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median methods reflects inherent uncertainty: the peer set skews later-stage, introducing upside bias, while the stage-progression method relies on raised capital as a valuation proxy, which understates value creation. Key uncertainties include First Resonance's relative progress versus peers on product traction and path to Series B pricing. A narrower range of $200M–$600M may be more defensible pending additional data on customer adoption and unit economics.
